final_rationale: The verdict does not change because the Actor provided no new admissible evidence; the response mainly reframed the same record more narrowly and conceded that clean policy compliance is not established. That narrower framing improves precision, but it does not cure the core defect: the available evidence still shows a potentially material named-use-case gap, an open legal disclosure review, and no evidence of either completed disclosure or approved risk acceptance. Because the unresolved caveat is itself a mandatory compliance predicate rather than a minor qualification, this remains noncompliant rather than compliant_with_caveats. Business-cost arguments and aggregate-readiness arguments are not admissible substitutes for satisfying the policy condition.
remaining_concerns: No new admissible evidence resolves whether the enterprise refund workflow gap requires disclosure under the release policy.
No admissible evidence shows completed disclosure or an approved risk acceptance for this specific gap before launch.
The affected workflow is tied to a named launch use case or customer commitment, which keeps materiality live under the policy text.
Aggregate readiness and absence of severity-one incidents do not satisfy the separate disclosure-or-risk-acceptance predicate.
Public model-card and risk-management guidance support monitoring and documentation practices but do not replace the internal policy requirement.
